scope.later_controls: July1870 Benjamin and September1875 Emma; 1883 death register for candidate test

conclusions: The Cookstown mill report contains two Williams: a co-plaintiff and an uncle. The Drapersfield Benjamin was still acting in July 1870, after Benjamin-2059’s death. These accounts keep roles and compatible candidates visible without assuming that each role is a separate new person. The 1792 shipmaster, 1793 Kildress delegate and 1820 Belfast grocer remain unjoined; the 1875 Parsonstown marriage is a later family lead. All new-person drafts remain on HOLD until identity and duplicate checks resolve them.
John-2058’s parents remain unknown. No relationship upgrade and no live WikiTree edit.

records.reading: Wm. Glasgow, master of brig William; Oporto voyage.
records.assessment: Actual surname-bearing master, not merely ship name William. Larne candidate unproved.

records.reading: Wm. Glasgow, master of brig William; Bordeaux voyage.
records.assessment: Same vessel and named master; household still unproved.

records.reading: William Glasgow, Kildress delegate and subsequent chairman; meeting 16 January 1793.
records.assessment: Candidate Glasgow-2915; no father or wife in notice.

records.reading: Captain Glasgow of brig William returned from Petersburg with hemp and flax.
records.assessment: Surname is a captain’s name. William is the vessel name here; his forename is unstated. Probable continuity with named 1792 master.

records.reading: William Glasgow signed Belfast banks confidence notice dated 15 June 1820.
records.assessment: Compatible with Belfast grocer; signature alone does not establish that identity.

records.reading: William Glasgow removed from Rosemary Street to shop and stores at 34 Smith Street, Belfast; teas, sugars and groceries; notice dated 30 October.
records.assessment: Documented Belfast grocer; no inspected bridge to Cookstown men.

records.reading: William Glasgow received £5 from executors of Mrs Margaret Lynd, Cookstown, bequeathed for the Fever Hospital.
records.assessment: No age, family or business address; remains unassigned among Cookstown Williams.

records.reading: Mr William Glasgow rescued a child whose clothes were burning at Cookstown, rolling it in snow.
records.assessment: The child is unnamed and no relationship to William is stated. No age/family identification for William.

records.reading: William Glasgow died 21 January at Sandusky City, Ohio, age 55; formerly Killycurragh near Cookstown; ruling elder at First Cookstown before emigration.
records.assessment: Identified as Glasgow-1675. Preserve News-Letter age 55 alongside attributed Mercury age 56; not living uncle in 1858.

records.reading: William Glasgow Esq., Cookstown, retired from business; presentation at Imperial Hotel, Belfast, 1 January: silver ewer and cake basket.
records.assessment: Retired merchant Glasgow-3814 is a strong compatible candidate; kinship to 1858 partners remains unproved.

records.reading: Benjamin and William Glasgow v John Sloan; mill-water dispute, River Ardtrea. Earlier Glasgow and Woods firm: Robert Glasgow and James Woods. William Glasgow, uncle of plaintiffs, testified.
records.assessment: Two distinct Williams. Robert is father of singular present plaintiff, unspecified between Benjamin and William. Does not prove parents of John-2058.

records.reading: Continuation of Benjamin and William Glasgow v John Sloan; Benjamin approached Sloan about levels in 1856; jury awarded 6d damages and 6d costs.
records.assessment: Confirms same named partners; no ages or additional parental identification.

records.reading: Tin Tenement, Main Street, and Monrush town parks for sale at Cookstown; apply to Mr William Glasgow, Cookstown; notice dated 15 August 1861.
records.assessment: Unassigned same-name contact. No kinship or proof that William owned the entire property.

records.reading: House occupied by Joseph M’Cormick, formerly residence of late Robert Glasgow; apply to Benjamin and William Glasgow, Drapersfield Mills, Cookstown; notice dated 16 January.
records.assessment: Partners named. The former occupant Robert died before 16 January 1864, but identity with 1842 partner still requires a bridge.

records.reading: Cheque for £71 12s 7d drawn by Benjamin and William Glasgow in favour of John Finlay junior, mentioned in William Adair case.
records.assessment: Business partnership confirmed; age and relatives unstated. William Adair is another person.

records.reading: Benjamin Glasgow Esq., Drapersfield, Cookstown, contact for Eary House and lands auction, estate of late William Magee.
records.assessment: Contact, not explicitly executor. Matches the documented Drapersfield business context.

records.reading: Benjamin Glasgow Esq., of Drapersfield, granted use of a field for the 12 July Cookstown gathering.
records.assessment: Later identity control: current action after Benjamin-2059’s February death strongly distinguishes the two Benjamins.

records.reading: William Treacy, second son of Robert Treacy, married Emma, daughter of late William Alexander Glasgow, 4 September, St Thomas’s Church, Belfast; both of Parsonstown.
records.assessment: Later family lead, outside pre-1870 publication window. William groom is Treacy, not Glasgow.
